profiles.subject: Theotokos

overview.text: The Mother of God of the Sign is an iconographic type and also the title of particular venerated icons. The OCA’s November 27 entry treats the Novgorod icon and then distinguishes other local examples, including Kursk.

sourceRefs.locator: Section Weeping Icon of the Mother of God of the Sign at Novgorod

blocks.text: Mary is depicted with raised hands, while the child Christ appears before her breast within a mandorla. The OCA describes this circular or oval enclosure as a defining feature. The Novgorod example displayed here is one historical realization of the type.

blocks.text: The source dates the type’s appearance in Russia to the eleventh and twelfth centuries. Its Novgorod narrative concerns the siege of 1170: an arrow strikes the icon during a procession, tears appear, and the attackers are overcome. This is the Church’s account of the commemoration.

blocks.text: The same entry records an observance instituted in memory of the deliverance and describes the spread of venerated copies with local names, including the Kursk and Abalaka images. These are particular local icons sharing the Sign composition.
